belief: It's all up to me; I can't count on God to provide.
origins: People who grew up with unreliable adults often learn to rely only on themselves. A parent who lost jobs, a family that ran out of money, or a time when no one came to help can train a person to carry every burden alone. Some of us were also taught, “God helps those who help themselves,” which is not in the Bible, and which leaves us believing that provision rests on us.
teaches: Scripture does call us to work, and God often provides through our work. But it also says, “Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it.” “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding.” “Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you.” Jesus says to seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to us. We do our part, and God is the Provider behind it all.
self_statements: If I do not handle it, no one will.
I cannot rely on anyone, including God.
God helps those who help themselves.
I have to make it happen.
Rest is a luxury I cannot afford.
errors: Believing it is either all me or all God.
Assuming God is as unreliable as people who let me down.
Insisting that I should carry everything.
Imagining collapse if I let go for a moment.
questions: Who let me down in the past, and how have I carried that over to God?
Where did I get the idea that “God helps those who help themselves”?
What have I already received that I did not produce myself?
What would it look like to do my part and trust God with the rest?
What burden can I give to God today?
Where has God come through for me before?
truth: I can work hard and still depend on God. He is the Provider behind my work, and He invites me to cast my burdens on Him. I do my part, and I trust Him with what I cannot control.
hw_truths: I can do my part and trust Him with the rest.
I do not have to carry it all.
log: Each day, write one thing you will do and one thing you will hand to God.
actions: List what is yours to do and what only God can do.
Write five times God came through when you could not.
Pray Psalm 55:22 and name the burden aloud.
Take a real break and notice that God still holds things together.
prayer: Lord, I have tried to carry everything. Teach me to work faithfully and to trust You as my Provider. I cast my burdens on You today. Sustain me and my family. Amen.
hw_questions: Who let me down in the past?
What is only God’s to do?
What burden can I give Him?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will cast my burden on the Lord and He will sustain me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “It's all up to me; I can't count on God to provide.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
